articles.headline: AI infrastructure boom is starting to fray as physical-world constraints bite
articles.summary: Financial-market coverage says the huge bet on AI infrastructure is running into the economics of power, hardware, and physical deployment. For businesses, that points to higher infrastructure costs, slower expansion, and more uncertainty around when AI capacity will become widely available.

articles.headline: Agentic AI could reshape enterprise software economics and seat-based pricing
articles.summary: A consulting analysis says agentic AI can reduce direct user interaction with SaaS tools, potentially shifting how enterprise software is priced and consumed. Business buyers should watch for lower labor and cycle-time costs, but also for new inference and orchestration expenses that may change total cost of ownership.

articles.headline: China proposes new export restrictions on 40 technologies, including 23 tied to AI
articles.summary: China’s draft rules could restrict overseas transfer of advanced AI models, AI agents used in sensitive settings, and chip-design technologies. For businesses, the move raises compliance risk, could complicate cross-border AI deployment, and may add friction to supply chains and partnerships involving Chinese technology.
